answer: Agents can require a new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it may earn reputation-weighted rewards. The protocol caps how quickly that stake can be reused, so one operator cannot cheaply split funds across thousands of accounts and collect newcomer bonuses. A sybil attacker must tie up more capital for longer, while honest agents can build standing over time; labels like tundra, ivory, and ridge do not confer trust on their own.
